legend: Vasya started working in a machine vision company of IT City. Vasya's team creates software and hardware for identification of people by their face.

One of the project's know-how is a camera rotating around its optical axis on shooting. People see an eye-catching gadget — a rotating camera — come up to it to see it better, look into it. And the camera takes their photo at that time. What could be better for high quality identification?

But not everything is so simple. The pictures from camera appear rotated too (on clockwise camera rotation frame the content becomes rotated counter-clockwise). But the identification algorithm can work only with faces that are just slightly deviated from vertical.

Vasya was entrusted to correct the situation — to rotate a captured image so that image would be minimally deviated from vertical. Requirements were severe. Firstly, the picture should be rotated only on angle divisible by 90 degrees to not lose a bit of information about the image. Secondly, the frames from the camera are so huge and FPS is so big that adequate rotation speed is provided by hardware FPGA solution only. And this solution can rotate only by 90 degrees clockwise. Of course, one can apply 90 degrees turn several times but for the sake of performance the number of turns should be minimized.

Help Vasya implement the program that by the given rotation angle of the camera can determine the minimum number of 90 degrees clockwise turns necessary to get a picture in which up direction deviation from vertical is minimum.
The next figure contains frames taken from an unrotated camera, then from rotated 90 degrees clockwise, then from rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise. Arrows show direction to "true up".
The next figure shows 90 degrees clockwise turn by FPGA hardware.
input: The only line of the input contains one integer x ( - 1018 ≤ x ≤ 1018) — camera angle in degrees. Positive value denotes clockwise camera rotation, negative — counter-clockwise.
output: Output one integer — the minimum required number of 90 degrees clockwise turns.
note: When the camera is rotated 60 degrees counter-clockwise (the second example), an image from it is rotated 60 degrees clockwise. One 90 degrees clockwise turn of the image result in 150 degrees clockwise total rotation and deviation from "true up" for one turn is 150 degrees. Two 90 degrees clockwise turns of the image result in 240 degrees clockwise total rotation and deviation from "true up" for two turns is 120 degrees because 240 degrees clockwise equal to 120 degrees counter-clockwise. Three 90 degrees clockwise turns of the image result in 330 degrees clockwise total rotation and deviation from "true up" for three turns is 30 degrees because 330 degrees clockwise equal to 30 degrees counter-clockwise.
From 60, 150, 120 and 30 degrees deviations the smallest is 30, and it it achieved in three 90 degrees clockwise turns.

legend.ai: Vasya 开始在 IT City 的一家机器视觉公司工作。Vasya 的团队开发用于通过人脸识别人们的软件和硬件。
该项目的一项独门技术是在拍摄时让摄像机绕其光轴旋转。人们看到这个引人注目的装置——一台旋转的摄像机——便会走近它，以便看得更清楚，并向镜头中看去。此时摄像机会拍下他们的照片。还有什么能比这更有利于高质量的人脸识别呢？
但并非一切都这么简单。摄像头拍摄的画面也会出现旋转（当摄像头顺时针旋转时，画面内容会逆时针旋转）。但识别算法只能处理那些与竖直方向偏差很小的面部。
Vasya 受委托来纠正这种情况——旋转捕获的图像，使图像与竖直方向的偏差最小。要求非常严格。首先，图像只能旋转 90 度的整数倍角度，以免丢失关于图像的任何信息。其次，摄像头输出的帧非常大，FPS 又很高，因此只有硬件 FPGA 方案才能提供足够的旋转速度，而该方案只能顺时针旋转 90 度。当然，可以多次施加 90 度旋转，但为了性能，旋转次数应尽可能少。
帮助 Vasya 实现一个程序：给定摄像头的旋转角度，计算最少需要进行多少次顺时针 90 度旋转，才能得到一幅“上方方向”与竖直方向偏差最小的图像。
下图展示了分别由未旋转的摄像头、顺时针旋转 90 度的摄像头、逆时针旋转 90 度的摄像头拍摄的帧。箭头指向“真正的上方”。
下图展示了 FPGA 硬件执行的顺时针 90 度旋转。

input.ai: 输入的唯一一行包含一个整数 x（-10^18 ≤ x ≤ 10^18）——以度为单位的相机角度。正值表示相机顺时针旋转，负值表示逆时针旋转。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——所需的最少 90 度顺时针旋转次数。

note.ai: 当相机逆时针旋转 60 度时（第二个样例），拍摄出的图像会顺时针旋转 60 度。将图像顺时针旋转 90 度一次后，总旋转角度为顺时针 150 度，此时相对于“正上方”的偏差为 150 度。将图像顺时针旋转 90 度两次后，总旋转角度为顺时针 240 度，此时相对于“正上方”的偏差为 120 度，因为顺时针旋转 240 度等价于逆时针旋转 120 度。将图像顺时针旋转 90 度三次后，总旋转角度为顺时针 330 度，此时相对于“正上方”的偏差为 30 度，因为顺时针旋转 330 度等价于逆时针旋转 30 度。
在 60、150、120 和 30 度的偏差中，最小的是 30 度，并且进行三次 90 度顺时针旋转即可达到这一偏差。
